sources.entry: Signature PDF - Sign and manipulate PDFs with collaboration, organization, compression and metadata editing. (Demo) AGPL-3.0 PHP/deb/Docker

summary.one_liner: Signature PDF is free, self-hostable web software for signing PDFs (alone or with others), organizing pages, editing metadata, and compressing PDFs.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a web application for signing PDFs, alone or with multiple signers, and for organizing them by merging, sorting, rotating, deleting, or extracting pages. It also covers editing PDF metadata and compressing PDFs. Multi-signature mode requires PDFs to be stored on the server, optionally encrypted with GPG. Digital signing uses pdfsig (poppler-utils) and certutil (libnss3-tools) with certificates in an NSS database. Configuration is done through config/config.ini, including retention periods for shared PDFs, default metadata fields, and disabling the Organize mode. The README lists many public instances run by various organizations.
use_cases: merge, sort or split PDF pages
digitally sign PDFs with a certificate
notable: Multi-signature mode where several people sign the same PDF, with PDFs stored on the server
Optional encrypted storage of PDFs on the server using GPG with a key known only to signers
Digital signature support via NSS certificate database and pdfsig
Configurable retention period for shared PDFs and default metadata fields
Many public instances are listed, so it can be used without self-hosting
caveats: Multi-signature mode requires storing PDFs on the server and configuring a writable storage folder
Digital signature needs extra system packages (poppler-utils, libnss3-tools) and certificate setup
Installation options listed in the README include Debian/Ubuntu, Docker, Linux Alpine and a package, but details are not given in this README excerpt
